Explore the repo /home/nick/work/andesim (search breadth: very thorough). Goal: understand the C++ driver (`driver/`) well enough to plan adding a new `profile` subcommand that (like `--mode hybrid`) requires picking a vsim engine and passes that engine's QEMU config to a QEMU launch.

Report back:
1. CLI plumbing: `driver/cli.hpp`, `driver/cli.cpp`, `driver/main.cpp` — how subcommands are declared/parsed/dispatched (the `is_subcommand` list at cli.cpp:30, defaulting to run at cli.cpp:49, usage/help blocks in main.cpp:100-160, dispatch at main.cpp:196-198). What fields struct Cli has, how options are parsed (per-subcommand or global?), how `--engine`, `--mode`, `--trigger`, `--mem-size` etc. are represented. How help text per subcommand works (print_run_block/print_list_block/print_doctor_block).
2. Engine selection + QEMU-config passing on the hybrid path: trace `driver/cmd_run.cpp` end-to-end for `--mode hybrid`. Specifically: how an engine is chosen/validated (`engine_registry.cpp/.hpp`, `engine_descriptor.hpp` — what fields an engine descriptor has: qemu_cpu? readconfig? mem sizes? describe output?), how the QEMU leg's argv is composed (`run_plan.cpp/.hpp`, `plan.hpp`, `memmap.cpp`, `shm.cpp`, `run_passthrough.cpp`) — which parts inject the engine's qemu cfg (-cpu, -readconfig file generation, -global, plugin args ilm_size/dlm_size/hvm_size, memory-backend-file/shared mmap), and which parts are hybrid-only (vsim leg, state files, verify). Also how `--mode fast` (QEMU-only) differs: does fast mode take an engine today?
3. How the driver locates QEMU binary + plugin .so paths (config.env / config_env.hpp, repo_root.hpp, setup.sh exports), and how it launches processes (`process.cpp/.hpp`) and captures output (`log.cpp`, output.log?).
4. `cmd_list.cpp` + `models.hpp`: what `list models|engines` shows, how engines are enumerated (VSIM_BIN_DIR sim_* scan? --describe?), so `profile` can reuse the same engine resolution.
5. Driver test conventions: driver/*_test.cpp files (cli_test.cpp, run_test.cpp, plan_test.cpp, plan_itest.cpp, infra_test.cpp) — test framework used (test_check.hpp? doctest?), how they're built/run (driver/CMakeLists.txt test targets, scripts/test_all.sh), plus the shell-test convention tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (pick 1-2 representative ones and summarize structure). This is needed because the project mandates TDD.
6. docs/USER_GUIDE.md sections describing the driver commands (run/list/doctor) — section numbers/structure so a new profile section fits in.
Include exact file paths and line numbers for the load-bearing spots.

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor). The single source of
26	// truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's dispatch.
27	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
28	
29	struct Cli {
30	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
31	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
32	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
33	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
34	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
35	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
36	  // parsed where they are used.
37	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
38	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
39	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
40	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
41	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
42	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
43	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
44	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
45	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
46	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
47	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
48	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
49	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
50	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
51	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
52	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
53	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
54	};
55	
56	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
57	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
58	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
59	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
60	
61	}  // namespace andes_sim
62	
63	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6), minus the dropped QEMU2
2	// step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	  // The engine whose hardware the fast leg(s) must model when the plan has
50	  // NO accurate-leg step of its own (the --verify oracle plan): the ISA sync
51	  // ({vlen}, {qemu_cpu}, -readconfig, LM sidecars) reads this engine instead.
52	  // Empty => derive from the plan's accurate-leg step (the normal case).
53	  std::string hw_engine_id;
54	};
55	
56	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
57	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
58	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
59	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
60	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
61	struct PhaseResult {
62	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
63	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
64	  std::string out;
65	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
66	};
67	
68	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
69	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
70	struct PlanResult {
71	  std::string error;
72	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
73	  // The concrete per-step argv run_plan built (after placeholder fill, qemu_cfg
74	  // staging, and state threading). Populated whether or not the steps spawn, so
75	  // a --dry-run can print the exact commands without executing them.
76	  std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> argvs;
77	  // On a leg failure: where the kept evidence lives (the workdir's drain/
78	  // sidecar/cfg files, a copy of the ELF, manifest.txt). Empty on success or
79	  // when the bundle could not be written.
80	  std::string repro_dir;
81	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
82	};
83	
84	}  // namespace andes_sim
85	
86	#endif  // ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
87

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- there is no QEMU2 handback leg.
2	// run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	#include "process.hpp"
18	
19	namespace andes_sim {
20	
21	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
22	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
23	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
24	struct RuntimeCtx {
25	  std::string mmap_path;
26	  long long mem_size = 0;
27	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
28	  std::string plugin_path;
29	  // QEMU `-readconfig` file matching the accurate engine's ISA, distilled from
30	  // its config.inc (the engine's `--print-qemu-config`). Empty => the fast leg
31	  // keeps its descriptor's default `-cpu` (engines without the flag; FA2).
32	  std::string qemu_cfg;
33	  // The QEMU CPU model the fast leg must instantiate ({qemu_cpu} fill),
34	  // parsed from the same probe's `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` globals: the
35	  // readconfig globals only apply to THAT driver, and a mismatched model
36	  // silently ignores them (found live: andes-ax45mpv kept vlen=512 when the
37	  // ax66 run asked for 128). Empty => the family default (andes-ax45mpv).
38	  std::string qemu_cpu;
39	};
40	
41	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
42	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
43	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
44	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
45	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
46	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
47	}
48	
49	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
50	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
51	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
52	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
53	// themselves).
54	struct LegTriggerArgs {
55	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
56	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
57	};
58	
59	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
60	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. Roles other
61	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
62	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
63	//
64	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
65	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
66	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
67	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
68	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
69	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
70	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
71	                                std::string& err);
72	
73	// Turn an accurate engine's `<bin> --print-qemu-config` probe into a QEMU
74	// `-readconfig` file under `workdir`. On a clean probe (exit 0, non-empty
75	// stdout) writes `workdir/qemu.cfg` and returns its path; on any failure
76	// (engine without the flag -> the parser throws -> non-zero exit; timeout;
77	// spawn failure; empty output; unwritable dir) returns "" -- the tolerant
78	// fallback that leaves the fast leg on its descriptor's default -cpu.
79	std::string stage_qemu_cfg(const std::string& workdir, const RunResult& probe);
80	
81	// The QEMU CPU model named by a `--print-qemu-config` probe's text: the first
82	// `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` global, stripped of the "-riscv-cpu" suffix.
83	// "" when the text names none (probe failed / engine without the hook) -- the
84	// caller falls back to the family-default -cpu.
85	std::string qemu_cpu_from_cfg(const std::string& cfg_text);
86	
87	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
88	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
89	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
90	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
91	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
92	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
93	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
94	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
95	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
96	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
97	
98	// The exit code a leg returns after draining its state and handing off (the
99	// driver-side mirror of vsim's kExitHandoffToQemu). Every plan step is a drain
100	// step, so this is the expected per-leg exit.
101	constexpr int kDrainRc = 200;
102	
103	struct PlanOptions {
104	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
105	  int expect_rc = kDrainRc;   // drain success code
106	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
107	  bool dry_run = false;       // build argvs (incl. qemu_cfg) but spawn nothing
108	};
109	
110	// Compose the "plan step N exited wrong" diagnostic. A drain step (expect_rc is
111	// the handoff/drain code) that exits 0 ran the ELF to completion without ever
112	// reaching its ROI boundary -- the marker/pc trigger never fired; say so and
113	// name the trigger kind so the fix (right ELF / right --trigger) is obvious.
114	// Any other mismatch gets the plain "expected X, got Y" line.
115	std::string plan_step_rc_error(size_t step, const Step& s, int expect_rc,
116	                               int got_rc);
117	
118	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
119	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
120	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
121	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
122	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
123	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
124	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
125	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
126	
127	}  // namespace andes_sim
128	
129	#endif  // ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

1	// The hybrid guest memory map: which regions a workload may touch in
2	// `run --mode hybrid`, composed from the same sources the run itself trusts.
3	//
4	// Only hybrid-SUPPORTED regions appear (PM rule): regions modeled by BOTH
5	// engines whose content or device behavior the handoff actually provides.
6	// QEMU-only devices (MROM/PLIC/PLMT/virtio/...), vsim-reserved holes (PLDM),
7	// and unverified-parity devices (UART1/SMU) are deliberately absent.
8	//
9	// Sources, in provenance order:
10	//   - DRAM + V-scratch: the driver's own window math (--mem-size; the
11	//     reserved HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES page above program RAM, L26).
12	//   - ILM/DLM/HVM bases: the engine's `--print-qemu-config` text -- the same
13	//     staged qemu.cfg the QEMU fast leg boots with, so the printed bases are
14	//     exactly the run's effective geometry.
15	//   - ILM/DLM/HVM sizes + row presence: the engine descriptor's backdoor-gated
16	//     ilm/dlm/hvm_size (0 = content cannot cross the handoff -> row omitted).
17	//   - SimControl/HTIF + UART2: fixed AE350 platform constants, identical in
18	//     QEMU (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c memmap table) and vsim (platform
19	//     memory_map.h); drift is guarded by tests/andes_sim/
20	//     test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh, which cross-checks the engine's own
21	//     `--print-memmap` dump.
22	//   - L2C register window (0xe0500000): intentionally absent until an engine
23	//     ships with an L2C -- `--describe` carries no L2C capability today, and
24	//     every current engine is built _NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0.
25	#ifndef ANDESIM_MEMMAP_HPP
26	#define ANDESIM_MEMMAP_HPP
27	
28	#include <cstdint>
29	#include <map>
30	#include <string>
31	#include <vector>
32	
33	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
34	
35	namespace andes_sim {
36	
37	struct MemmapRow {
38	  std::string region;     // "DRAM", "V-scratch", "ILM", ...
39	  uint64_t base = 0;      // guest physical, first byte
40	  uint64_t end = 0;       // guest physical, LAST byte (inclusive)
41	  std::string transport;  // what the handoff does with the region's content
42	};
43	
44	struct MemmapResult {
45	  std::vector<MemmapRow> rows;
46	  std::vector<std::string> warnings;  // e.g. LM geometry unavailable
47	};

49	// Extract the `riscv.andes.ae350.soc` [global] properties from an engine's

53	    const std::string& cfg_text);
54	
55	// Compose the hybrid map for `eng` with `mem_size` bytes of program RAM

61	// "128M" / "4K" / "2G" for whole binary multiples, plain decimal bytes else.

1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andesim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;
19	
20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};
33	
34	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);

40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)

43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own

1	// Subprocess helpers for andesim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.
7	#ifndef ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <functional>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <string_view>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	struct RunResult {
18	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
19	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
20	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
21	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
22	};
23	
24	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
25	// is redirected to /dev/null; stderr too, unless relay_stderr is set, in
26	// which case the child inherits OUR stderr and its diagnostics stream live
27	// (used to surface the legs' leveled logs at --log-level <= debug). If the
28	// child runs longer than timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
29	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms,
30	                      bool relay_stderr = false);
31	
32	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
33	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
34	// `run --mode fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
35	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
36	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
37	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
38	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
39	
40	// Fork a child that execs argv with inherited stdio and return immediately
41	// without waiting. Used by `run --mode cycle --gdb` to launch vsim in the
42	// background before exec-ing ICEman in the foreground. Returns the child pid
43	// on success, -1 on empty argv or fork failure.
44	int fork_background(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
45	
46	// Run argv with BOTH stdout and stderr captured (separate pipes) and stdin
47	// inherited, streaming each complete line to `on_line(stream, line)` as it
48	// arrives -- stream is 1 (stdout) or 2 (stderr), line excludes the trailing
49	// newline. The callback owns presentation (it decides what to write to the real
50	// streams), so this is the filtered counterpart to exec_passthrough: same "run
51	// to completion, no timeout, propagate exit code" contract, but the parent sees
52	// every line. A final unterminated line is delivered too. Returns the child's
53	// exit code, 128+signal if signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
54	int run_line_filtered(
55	    const std::vector<std::string>& argv,
56	    const std::function<void(int stream, std::string_view line)>& on_line);
57	
58	}  // namespace andes_sim
59	
60	#endif  // ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP

1	// andesim leveled logging.
2	//
3	// The scale mirrors the vsim engines' --log-level option so users learn one
4	// scheme: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off. A message
5	// prints when its level >= the threshold; the default threshold is info.
6	//
7	// What lives at which level (driver policy):
8	//   info  -- the answers: program output relays, the cycle figure,
9	//            --dry-run/--verify results. Program output itself is never
10	//            gated (it is the program's, not a log).
11	//   debug -- driver chatter: the hybrid banner, the mmap line, PASS lines,
12	//            verify progress notes.
13	//   warn  -- degradations: unsupported-CSR warnings, skipped engines.
14	// Fatal errors are not gated: they accompany a non-zero exit.
15	#ifndef ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
16	#define ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
17	
18	#include <string>
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	enum LogLevel {
23	  kLogTrace = 0,
24	  kLogDebug = 1,
25	  kLogInfo = 2,
26	  kLogWarn = 3,
27	  kLogError = 4,
28	  kLogCritical = 5,
29	  kLogOff = 6,
30	};
31	
32	// Set the process-wide threshold from the CLI value. "" keeps the default
33	// (info). Returns false (and leaves the threshold alone) when the value is
34	// not an integer in 0..6.
35	bool set_log_threshold(const std::string& cli_value);
36	
37	// The current threshold (0..6). Used to forward the level to child engines.
38	int log_threshold();
39	
40	// True when a message at `level` should print.
41	bool log_on(int level);
42	
43	// Open the --log-file sink. Once open, EVERY log_line/log_result message --
44	// all levels, even below the console threshold -- is appended to the file
45	// with a UTC timestamp and a level tag. Returns false if the file cannot be
46	// opened (the sink stays off). Empty path is a no-op success.
47	bool set_log_file(const std::string& path);
48	
49	// The open sink's path, or "" when none.
50	const std::string& log_file_path();
51	
52	// Emit one chatter line to stderr when `level` passes the threshold. Pass
53	// the complete line text (including its "[andesim] " prefix), without the
54	// trailing newline. Always mirrored to the --log-file sink.
55	void log_line(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
56	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
57	
58	// Emit one RESULT line (the cycle figure, PASS/verify verdicts) to stdout
59	// when `level` passes the threshold. Always mirrored to the sink.
60	void log_result(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
61	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
62	
63	}  // namespace andes_sim
64	
65	#endif  // ANDESIM_LOG_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
  done
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

1	# Engine interface
2	
3	How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.
4	
5	`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
6	one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
7	`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
8	`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
9	the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
10	know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
11	zero per-engine code in the framework.
12	
13	To join, an engine does two things:
14	
15	1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
16	2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
17	   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
18	   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
19	   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.
20	
21	## 1. The `--describe` JSON
22	
23	Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
24	and exit 0. Example (Verilator):
25	
26	```json
27	{
28	  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
29	  "type":     "verilator",
30	  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
31	  "vlen":     512,
32	  "dlen":     512,
33	  "elen":     32,
34	  "xlen":     64,
35	  "ilm_size": 65536,
36	  "dlm_size": 32768,
37	  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
38	  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
39	  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
40	  "andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "jvt"],
41	  "invoke": {
42	    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
43	    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
44	                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
45	                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
46	                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
47	                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
48	                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
49	  },
50	  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
51	}
52	```
53	
54	The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.
55	
56	### Fields

# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "dlen":     512,
  "elen":     32,
  "xlen":     64,
  "ilm_size": 65536,
  "dlm_size": 32768,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "jvt"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `ilm_size` | number          | no       | Hart-0 ILM size in BYTES (0 / omit = none). When > 0, a hybrid run drains the ILM content to a `<state>.ilm` sidecar on the fast leg and feeds it to the accurate leg via `--ilm` (same for `dlm_size`/`--dlm`). |
| `dlm_size` | number          | no       | Hart-0 DLM size in BYTES (0 / omit = none). |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

### Roles

- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `cycle` models).
  Transparent passthrough: `andesim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
  the reported cycle figure.

### invoke + placeholders

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
tokens when it builds the command:

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
| `{mmap_size}` | the shared-mmap size in bytes |
| `{mmap_base}` | the guest physical base address of the mmap (e.g. `0x0`) |
| `{vlen}`      | the synced VLEN (bits) from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor |
| `{plugin}`    | the TCG plugin path (fast-leg only) |
| `{plugin_args}` | the plugin comma-suffix: trigger args (e.g. `,enter_pc=0xADDR` for pc; empty for marker) plus, when the accurate engine reports local memories, the LM sidecar-drain args (`,ilm_size=N,dlm_size=N`) |
| `{trigger}`   | compatibility alias of `{plugin_args}` (the name predates non-trigger plugin args); same value |

`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
appended.

### result

Declares where an engine's standalone measurement lives. `stderr:<word>`
advertises that the figure is the integer next to `<word>` on stderr (vsim
prints `<n> cycles simulated`); `state.mcycle` advertises the `mcycle` field of
the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.

NOTE: the current driver does not yet act on this field. Standalone runs
(`fast`/`cycle`) pass the engine's stdout/stderr/exit code through verbatim, and
hybrid runs always read the cycle figure as the accurate-leg `mcycle` delta from
the drained state files. The field is parsed into the descriptor for forward
compatibility, not consumed.

## 2. ABI conformance

Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.

## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)

`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
shares it:

1. The built-in `qemu64` (rv64) and `qemu32` (rv32) descriptors are always
   present (QEMU does not implement `--describe`; their binary paths honor
   `$VSIM_QEMU` / `$VSIM_QEMU32`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
2. The scan directory is:
   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.

Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.

## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)

1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.
5. **(Optional) QEMU ISA match**: implement `--print-qemu-config` to emit a QEMU `-readconfig` cfg (per-extension `[global]` properties) describing your engine's ISA, so a hybrid run's QEMU fast leg executes the same extensions you model. On a hybrid run the framework runs `<accurate-engine> --print-qemu-config` and passes the result to QEMU via `-readconfig`. If you do not implement it (the flag exits non-zero), the framework falls back to QEMU's default `-cpu` -- no error. vsim bakes this cfg from its `config.inc` at build time.

226	## 5. The `run` options, one by one
227	
228	Synopsis:
229	
230	```
231	./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
232	```
233	
234	`run` is the default command -- you may omit it. `./andesim --mode fast
235	my.elf` and `./andesim my.elf --mode fast` both work; only the explicit
236	commands (`list`, `doctor`) are recognized by name.
237	
238	### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)
239	
240	Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.
241	
242	### 5.2 `--engine <id>`
243	
244	Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.
245	
246	- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
247	  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
248	  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
249	- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
250	  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:
251	
252	  ```
253	  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
254	  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
255	  ```
256	
257	Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
258	engine, up front:
259	
260	```
261	andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
262	  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
263	```
264	
265	Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
266	engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).
267	
268	VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
269	mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
270	both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
271	128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
272	`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
273	VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
274	wins):
275	
276	```sh
277	./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
278	```
279	
280	### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required
281	
282	The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.
283	
284	**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
285	window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
286	`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
287	cost nothing.
288	
289	**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
290	required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:
291	
292	```sh
293	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
294	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
295	```
296	
297	Semantics you should know:
298	
299	- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
300	  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
301	  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
302	  closes.
303	- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
304	  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
305	  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
306	  `malformed address '<x>'`.
307	- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
308	  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
309	  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
310	- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
311	  empty window and is rejected up front:
312	  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.
313	
314	### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory
315	
316	`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:
317	
318	| Model    | Effect |
319	|----------|--------|
320	| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
321	| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
322	| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |
323	
324	Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
325	map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
326	headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:
327	
328	1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
329	2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
330	
331	```
332	[andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
333	```
334	
335	Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
336	(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
337	tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
338	still RAM.
339	
340	### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?
341	
342	Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
343	`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
344	then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.

engine, up front:

```
andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
```

Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).

VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
wins):

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
```

### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required

The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.

**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
cost nothing.

**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
```

Semantics you should know:

- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
  closes.
- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
  `malformed address '<x>'`.
- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
  empty window and is rejected up front:
  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.

### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory

`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:

| Model    | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |

Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:

1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).

```
[andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
```

Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
still RAM.

### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?

Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.

1. Validate cheaply first: ELF (`check_one_elf`/`abs_elf` at cmd_run.cpp:54-90), trigger (`hybrid_trigger`, cmd_run.cpp:402), vsim extras (`vsim_extra_args`, cmd_run.cpp:408), `--mem-size` cap (cmd_run.cpp:412-426, `max_program_mem_bytes`), and the V-scratch overlap guard (cmd_run.cpp:438-453).
2. **`Discovery disc = discover_engines();` (cmd_run.cpp:457)** then **`resolve_accurate_engine(disc.engines, cli.engine, err)` (cmd_run.cpp:458-465)** — the engine pick. Then `hybrid_hw_check` (rv64-only, cmd_run.cpp:469) and `elf_engine_arch_error` (cmd_run.cpp:471).
3. Build a 2-step `Plan` (cmd_run.cpp:504-521): `Step{kQemuId64,"fast-leg",trig}` + `Step{acc->id,"accurate-leg",trig}`; vsim-only extras appended (`--drain-minimal` unless `--verify`, `--log-level`).
4. `run_plan(plan, disc.engines, opts)` (cmd_run.cpp:536).

**QEMU-config injection — `driver/run_plan.cpp` (this is the load-bearing mechanism `profile` must copy):**
- **`run_plan` (run_plan.cpp:337-448)**: allocates the shared mmap (`allocate(physical_mmap_bytes(...))`, run_plan.cpp:347-357), makes a workdir (mkdtemp, 360-371), fills `RuntimeCtx` (373-380). Then at **run_plan.cpp:388-396** it probes the hw-reference engine: `run_process({e->bin_path, "--print-qemu-config"}, kQemuCfgProbeMs)` → **`stage_qemu_cfg(wd, probe)`** (writes `workdir/qemu.cfg`, run_plan.cpp:144-152) → sets `ctx.qemu_cfg`, and **`qemu_cpu_from_cfg(probe.out)`** (parses the `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` global, run_plan.cpp:126-142) → `ctx.qemu_cpu`. Which engine is the hw reference is decided by `plan_hw_engine` (run_plan.cpp:116-124): the first `accurate-leg` step's engine, or `plan.hw_engine_id` for a leg-less oracle plan.
- **`plan_argvs` (run_plan.cpp:224-335)** fills templates via `build_argv`:
  - vlen/ILM/DLM/HVM sync read from the hw engine's descriptor (run_plan.cpp:233-249); `synced_vlen` fallback 512.
  - The `{plugin_args}`/`{trigger}` comma-suffix (trigger args + `,ilm_size=…,dlm_size=…,hvm_size=…` + `,log_level=…`) built at run_plan.cpp:279-281, placed in the ctx map (282-297) along with `{qemu_cpu}` (defaulting to `andes-ax45mpv`) and `{vlen}`.
  - **`-readconfig <cfg>` is appended to the fast-leg only** at run_plan.cpp:306-309 (`if step.role=="fast-leg" && !ctx.qemu_cfg.empty()`).
  - `--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` sidecars appended to the **accurate-leg only** at run_plan.cpp:312-325.
- Note: there is no literal `-global` argv token — the per-extension globals live *inside* the generated `qemu.cfg` loaded by `-readconfig`; the CPU model is set via `-cpu {qemu_cpu},vlen={vlen}` in the template.
- The spawn loop (run_plan.cpp:414-442) runs each leg with a timeout, requires `expect_rc == 200` (`kDrainRc`, run_plan.hpp:101), reads back each drained `hybrid_state_v1` via `read_state_file`. `--dry-run` builds argvs but spawns nothing (run_plan.cpp:403-406).

**Which parts are hybrid-only (NOT needed by a profile-style QEMU-only launch):** the vsim `accurate-leg` step and its `--resume-from-qemu`/`--handoff-out`/`--shared-mem-*` template (`docs/engine_interface.md:43-49`), state-file threading (`state_path`, run_plan.cpp:26-28; `driver/state.hpp`), the drain exit-code contract (`kDrainRc`), `--drain-minimal`, the `--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` sidecar load, the `--verify` oracle plan (cmd_run.cpp:605-651, `driver/state_diff.cpp`), the repro bundle (run_plan.cpp:51-91), and the V-scratch page reservation (`physical_mmap_bytes`). A `profile` that is a **single QEMU launch with the engine's cfg** needs only: engine resolution → `--print-qemu-config` probe → `stage_qemu_cfg`/`qemu_cpu_from_cfg` → one QEMU argv with `-readconfig` + `-cpu {qemu_cpu},vlen={vlen}` + `-plugin <profiler.so>` + `-bios {elf}`. That probe+stage+cpu logic currently lives *inside* `run_plan` (run_plan.cpp:388-396) — to reuse it for a non-plan launch you'd call `run_process`/`stage_qemu_cfg`/`qemu_cpu_from_cfg` directly (they're already exported in run_plan.hpp:73-85), exactly as `run_hybrid`'s `--print-memmap` branch already does at **cmd_run.cpp:479-487**.

**Does `--mode fast` take an engine today? — `run_fast` (cmd_run.cpp:192-233):** No vsim engine. `--engine` is accepted but **must be `qemu64` or `qemu32`** (rejected otherwise at cmd_run.cpp:194-200); it resolves the built-in qemu descriptor directly (`builtin_qemu_arch(xlen)`, cmd_run.cpp:232) and never runs `--print-qemu-config`/`-readconfig`. It forwards only `--mem-size` as plain `-m` (`qemu_m_args`, cmd_run.cpp:204) and optional `--gdb` stub (cmd_run.cpp:210-215). So the "pick a vsim engine + pass its QEMU cfg" behavior is unique to the hybrid path today — `profile` is the second consumer.

- **Plugin .so:** `resolve_plugin` at **run_plan.cpp:101-105** → `$VSIM_PLUGIN` else `default_plugin_path()` = `repo_root()/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (**repo_root.hpp:55-57**).
- **config.env resolution:** `config_env_value` (env-first, then first `KEY=value` in `config.env`) at **config_env.hpp:22-45**; repo-root discovery via `/proc/self/exe` at **repo_root.hpp:22-49**.
- **`setup.sh`** exports `QEMU_BIN_DIR`, `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_QEMU32`, `VSIM_PLUGIN` at **setup.sh:133-143** (and builds `libhybrid_handoff.so`, setup.sh:112-120). `config.env` holds `QEMU_BIN_DIR`/`VSIM_BIN_DIR` (config.env:19-22).

The repo-root **`output.log` is a generated e2e artifact, not written by the driver's logger** (the logger only writes to a `--log-file` path).

- **`driver/cmd_list.cpp`:** `cmd_list` (173-188) dispatches `models`/`engines` (and `fixtures`, dev-gated via `is_dev_mode()`). `list_engines` (**cmd_list.cpp:142-169**) calls `discover_engines()` and prints `ENGINE/TYPE/KIND/XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN`, reporting `disc.warnings` for binaries that failed to self-describe. `list_models` (127-140) renders `kModels`.
- **`driver/models.hpp`:** `kModels[]` at **models.hpp:21-27** (`fast`/`cycle`/`hybrid` with engine-composition + notes); `find_model` at **models.hpp:29-33** (used by `cmd_run` at cmd_run.cpp:667 to validate `--mode`). If `profile` becomes a top-level command (not a mode) it does **not** need a `kModels` entry; if you ever expose `--mode profile` it would.
- **Engine enumeration path** is entirely `discover_engines()` → `sim_*` scan under `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (or any exe under `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR`) via `--describe`/sidecar. **`profile` reuses `discover_engines()` + `resolve_accurate_engine()` verbatim** — same resolution `cycle`/`hybrid` use, so `--engine vsim:<cfg>` and the sole-engine default work identically.

**Prior art worth mirroring:** `driver/hotloops.cpp` is a *separate* executable (CMake target `hotloops`, CMakeLists.txt:69), not a subcommand — a baremetal-ELF profiler that launches `qemu-system-*` with a TCG plugin and already has a **`--qemu-config <file>` → `-readconfig <file>`** knob (hotloops.cpp:15, :132, :769) and a full QEMU argv build at **hotloops.cpp:756-772** (`-plugin`, `-cpu`, `-machine andes_ae350`, `-nographic -semihosting`, `-bios {elf}`, then `-readconfig`). This is essentially the QEMU-leg shape a `profile` subcommand needs; the new work is wiring engine-derived cfg (`--print-qemu-config` → `stage_qemu_cfg`) into it instead of a user-passed file, and surfacing it as an `andesim profile` subcommand rather than a standalone binary.
